one_line: WebMCP-native trail planner for verified local hiking loops.
what_it_does: Lets a person and agent find, validate, inspect, and prepare route briefings or GPX for Collserola walks on a shared map.
leverage_rationale: Shared spatial state, graph-verified circuits, route validation, and visible evidence make the agent materially more reliable than generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text describes shared map, route ledger, worklog, graph-verified circuits, measured distance and ascent.
Frame sheet visibly shows a browser map workflow with highlighted geography and a generated scrollable report.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent map-to-report workflow with branded UI and concrete route outputs, though no live video and limited legibility constrain end-to-end certainty.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows form/setup, map interaction, highlighted route or boundary, and detailed categorized report states.
Demo is marked alive and four gallery images are reported.
impact_rationale: It addresses a specific real planning problem for hikers and trail runners: finding accessible, current, safe loops instead of relying on unverified recommendations.
impact_evidence: About text identifies time pressure, closed hikes, dangerous segments, and the Collserola audience.
Product visibly combines geographic route selection with explanatory planning output.
creativity_rationale: The shared human-agent spatial planning and evidence ledger are a fresh treatment of a familiar route-planning category.
creativity_evidence: About text frames hiking as a shared spatial decision rather than a single text answer.
Agent actions render directly into an inspectable map and trail ledger.
usability_note: The workflow is visually structured, but small dense controls and unclear text legibility leave some usability details unverified.
red_flags: No submitted video; frame evidence is visually legible only at a high level.
Access model and origin are not established by the packet.
standouts: Ground-truth route validation on a shared map.
Human remains in control of GPX download and planning decisions.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP fit and credible niche impact, with coherent visual evidence despite missing video.

one_line: AI-assisted workspace for searching and creating UTM-tracked short links.
what_it_does: Exposes public QR and product tools plus signed-in link search, CRUD, and organization analytics through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: Structured access to authenticated org-scoped link and analytics operations improves repeatability, but a general agent could accomplish much of the same through the existing UI.
leverage_evidence: About text lists typed tools for search, create, edit, delete, QR generation, and analytics.
Tools call the same org-scoped REST endpoints and results land in the real UI.
execution_rationale: The claimed implementation is coherent and covers a substantial existing product surface, but packet evidence is thin and lacks video or gallery screenshots.
execution_evidence: Demo is marked alive.
About text describes Playwright testing with fake modelContext and explicit output limits/hints.
impact_rationale: Marketing and growth users have a clear need for tracked links and analytics, though the packet does not show a distinctive improvement beyond easier automation.
impact_evidence: Pitch directly targets UTM short-link creation and search.
Authenticated organization analytics and QR export are described.
creativity_rationale: It is a competent WebMCP integration of an established short-link product with limited novelty in the core concept.
creativity_evidence: The project explicitly says the underlying software already exists and WebMCP exposes normal actions.
Twelve tools cover familiar CRUD and generator workflows.
usability_note: The described real-UI results and public/signed-in separation are promising, but no visual evidence was submitted.
red_flags: No gallery images or video evidence.
Submission describes an already existing software product with zero new backend; origin is pre-existing, though WebMCP work is new.
standouts: Good authorization and graceful no-op behavior for unsupported browsers.
Explicit read-only and untrusted-content tool metadata.
advance_reason: Useful but largely conventional integration, with especially thin packet evidence.

one_line: Revision-safe shared offsite planning with human approval and exactly-once execution.
what_it_does: Coordinates attendee arrivals, agenda, meals, and reservations in a live human-agent plan with revision-bound capabilities and durable receipts.
leverage_rationale: The product makes shared live state, explicit authority, stale-capability rejection, and exactly-once execution central; generic UI driving cannot reliably reproduce those guarantees.
leverage_evidence: Transcript demonstrates revision-bound tools, stale rejection before mutation, human-only approval, and recoverable exactly-once receipt.
About text describes capability epochs bound to server revision and deterministic fingerprint.
execution_rationale: The 114-second video transcript and packet describe a complete conflict-to-repair-to-approval-to-reservation workflow with a deliberate stale replay proof.
execution_evidence: Transcript covers conflict discovery, two repairs, selected update, human authorization, reservation receipt, reload recovery, and rejected stale invocation.
Video is submitted and demo is alive; public repo is available.
impact_rationale: Chiefs of staff and offsite organizers face exactly the coordination and approval-drift problems demonstrated; the workflow provides credible safety and time value.
impact_evidence: Transcript specifies eight teammates with different arrival times and a concrete schedule conflict.
Human control over consequential approval and prevention of duplicate reservations directly address real operational risk.
creativity_rationale: Revision-bound authority epochs and stale-tool non-events are an unusually deep interaction model for human-agent workflow collaboration.
creativity_evidence: No authorize_plan tool exists by design; authority is kept with the human.
The packet makes causality and stale replay behavior explicit rather than merely claiming agent automation.
usability_note: The staged Inspect/Repair/Review/Reserve flow and visible authority boundaries should make a consequential workflow understandable.
standouts: Strongest safety model in the packet: revision binding, human authorization, stale rejection, exactly-once receipt.
Clear shared decision surface for human and agent.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and execution evidence, with high-impact and original workflow design.

one_line: Shared browser telemetry atlas for dependency, risk, and performance investigation.
what_it_does: Analyzes any public site in isolated Chromium, maps requests and initiators, focuses findings in a dashboard, and runs dependency-blocking experiments.
leverage_rationale: The agent operates on structured, measured browser evidence and can change the same visible analysis workspace; this is substantially more reliable than clicking through devtools.
leverage_evidence: About text describes isolated browser collection, dependency paths, focus actions, and before/after blocking experiments.
Frontend tools share Zustand state with the human dashboard.
execution_rationale: The architecture and workflow are coherent and ambitious, but the packet has no video and frame details are not available as transcript evidence.
execution_evidence: Demo alive, public repo, and 12-tool workflow are reported.
About text names React/Flow dashboard, Fastify Playwright backend, CDP, axe, and deployment.
impact_rationale: Web developers, security/privacy reviewers, and performance engineers have a real need to turn noisy dependency telemetry into actionable evidence.
impact_evidence: About text identifies slow, highly technical investigation of scripts, trackers, APIs, and third parties.
Blocking experiments connect diagnosis to measurable before-and-after effects.
creativity_rationale: Combining dependency graph investigation, agent-guided visible focus, and real browser experiments is a notably original devtools interaction.
creativity_evidence: The product treats browser loading as a shared, verifiable investigation workspace.
It combines network/runtime/accessibility/privacy evidence with controlled interventions.
usability_note: A bounded dashboard is promising, but usability and safety of arbitrary URL analysis are not visually verified here.
red_flags: No submitted video; end-to-end claims rely on description and architecture.
standouts: Real before/after dependency-blocking experiments.
Shared state between agent tool handlers and React Flow workspace.
advance_reason: Strong dev-tool concept with meaningful WebMCP delta and credible technical scope.

one_line: Collaborative construction document review that separates agent evidence work from human drawing judgment.
what_it_does: Lets agents search extracted PDF evidence and navigate a workbench while humans inspect drawings and answer structured assistance requests.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides structured evidence search, synchronized page/region navigation, and a human-agent handoff tailored to a domain where generic agents are unreliable.
leverage_evidence: About text describes search across extracted PDFs, jump-to-page/block/region, assistance requests, and structured human responses.
Fixed demo includes known fail and pass submittal cases.
execution_rationale: The packet gives a coherent domain workflow and seeded test cases, but no video and only one gallery image limit observed completeness.
execution_evidence: Demo alive and public repo are reported.
About text identifies real Virginia Farmhouse drawings, submittals, issues, and disposition flow.
impact_rationale: Construction review has a specific high-cost audience and clear risk from missed requirements, bid errors, and delayed submittals; the human-in-the-loop fit is credible.
impact_evidence: About text cites denied submittals adding weeks and bid errors costing hundreds of thousands.
Product intentionally keeps drawing interpretation with construction professionals.
creativity_rationale: The deliberate division of labor between agent evidence reconciliation and human visual judgment is a thoughtful, domain-specific interaction model.
creativity_evidence: The product refuses to ask agents to read plan symbols and linework alone.
Assistance Requests let the agent pause on uncertainty and resume from structured human input.
usability_note: The handoff model sounds clear, but visual interaction quality and accessibility are not verifiable without richer evidence.
red_flags: No video; end-to-end behavior is claimed rather than observed.
Demo is fixed-project rather than general document ingestion.
standouts: Strong human/agent division of labor for a high-stakes domain.
Known pass and fail cases enable credible evaluation.
advance_reason: High real-world impact and a well-justified WebMCP collaboration model.

one_line: Human-agent shared motorsport circuit design lab.
what_it_does: Humans edit and lock a visual circuit while agents inspect telemetry, reshape unlocked sectors, simulate races, compare snapshots, and export presentations.
leverage_rationale: Semantic circuit operations against exact live shared state, lock-aware edits, deterministic analysis, and simulation make WebMCP central rather than a UI automation convenience.
leverage_evidence: About text gives a real reshape_sector call receipted in Activity and says agents modify the exact same circuit.
Locked turns constrain agent changes while shared telemetry and simulation update with design.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a broad but coherent design-to-analysis workflow with references, locking, snapshots, simulation, and exports; no video lowers certainty.
execution_evidence: Ten gallery images are reported and demo is alive.
About text enumerates canvas, telemetry, Activity receipts, reference library, snapshots, race simulation, and export modes.
impact_rationale: Motorsport designers, game designers, and racing enthusiasts have a credible creative and analytical use case, though the audience is specialized.
impact_evidence: Product supports Formula 1, Formula E, and MotoGP references plus custom circuits.
Race-flow simulation turns design tradeoffs into testable signals.
creativity_rationale: The visual-human/semantic-agent circuit co-design model, lock semantics, and race-flow feedback are highly memorable and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Human designs visually while agent reshapes semantically around locked corners.
The project integrates circuit editing, deterministic telemetry, simulation, snapshots, and presentation export.
usability_note: The explicit division between visual editing and semantic tools suggests strong usability, though live interaction is not directly observed.
red_flags: No video; agent invocation and runtime robustness are not directly observed.
standouts: Lock-aware agent editing preserves human intent.
Unusually deep creative tool with simulation feedback.
advance_reason: Outstanding creativity and strong WebMCP-native shared-state concept.

one_line: Self-healing in-browser performance runtime with provenance for every fix.
what_it_does: Uses browser performance telemetry to detect and reversibly contain runtime problems, then records tamper-evident mutation provenance.
leverage_rationale: In-process WebMCP access lets the agent observe and remediate the active document without reload or server round trip, a meaningful capability delta over external automation.
leverage_evidence: About text claims direct PerformanceObserver access, DOM remediation, reversible CSS containment, and no reload.
Seven typed tools and awaited registration are described.
execution_rationale: The technical story is unusually specific, including measured latency change and provenance, but the absence of video makes the claimed repair end-to-end rather than observed.
execution_evidence: About text reports a legacy filter blocking ~470 ms and repaired input handler ~1 ms.
Demo alive, public repo, and two gallery images are reported.
impact_rationale: Web developers and users of heavy web applications benefit from reducing input latency and dropped frames without losing form state.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies concrete performance symptoms and evidence-gated repair.
No reload/lost state is a directly relevant benefit for interactive applications.
creativity_rationale: Combining autonomous runtime healing, browser-native telemetry, reversible mutation, and SLSA-shaped provenance is an ambitious and unusual concept.
creativity_evidence: Agent continuously inspects Long Animation Frame telemetry and hashes resulting DOM mutations.
The product positions the agent as an active runtime copilot rather than a diagnostic chatbot.
usability_note: Reversible, evidence-gated repairs are a good safety affordance, but user controls and failure states are not visually verified.
red_flags: No video; performance improvement and provenance claims are not independently observed in the packet.
SLSA wording is described as shaped rather than clearly standard-compliant.
standouts: No-reload in-process remediation.
Tamper-evident audit trail for agent mutations.
advance_reason: Technically distinctive performance-agent concept with credible value, despite limited execution evidence.

one_line: Multi-dimensional storefront negotiation between buyer and seller agents with human confirmation.
what_it_does: Lets agents negotiate price, quantity, add-ons, shipping, and coupons across a large catalog, then presents the settled deal for human confirmation.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives agents structured, page-local negotiation tools and shared cart/offer state; the multi-round deal interaction is materially beyond generic click automation.
leverage_evidence: About text lists search, product, cart, add-on, coupon, and negotiation tools registered on every page.
One OffersService mutation path enforces buyer budget and seller floor across buyer, seller, and auto-negotiator.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete multi-vendor negotiation and confirmation flow with explicit economic constraints, though no video limits observed proof.
execution_evidence: Demo alive, public repo, and three gallery images are reported.
About text claims 95k+ products, several rounds, confirm dialog, and no purchase before human confirmation.
impact_rationale: Shoppers and merchants have a real desire for better deals and less tedious bargaining; human confirmation addresses consequential purchase control.
impact_evidence: Pitch specifies concrete shopping dimensions beyond price.
Economic limits and confirmation boundary are explicitly implemented in the described flow.
creativity_rationale: Agent-to-agent bargaining over a multi-dimensional deal, with the human as final authority, is a memorable and ambitious commerce interaction.
creativity_evidence: The core concept is negotiation rather than merely search or checkout automation.
Buyer and seller agents negotiate several rounds while one pure transition function enforces constraints.
usability_note: The confirm dialog and in-page agent loop reduce setup friction, but actual interaction quality is not shown in video.
red_flags: No video; negotiation robustness and catalog breadth are claimed rather than directly observed.
standouts: Human confirmation remains mandatory.
Single constrained mutation path for all negotiation participants.
advance_reason: Highly creative WebMCP-native commerce flow with strong safety and credible audience value.

one_line: A commerce operations workspace that turns one human workflow demonstration into a reusable agent tool.
what_it_does: Records typed semantic business actions, lets a merchant review and parameterize them, publishes a routine, and exposes it as a discoverable WebMCP tool.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the mechanism that converts reviewed shared business actions into new agent capabilities without fixed developer integrations, making it central to the product thesis.
leverage_evidence: About text describes five typed verified actions captured from a real workflow and published as generate_weekly_report.
The generated tool executes in the live page and returns report ID, URL, summary, and receipts.
execution_rationale: The workflow is coherent and unusually complete on paper, but there is no video or gallery evidence to verify recording, review, publication, and invocation end-to-end.
execution_evidence: Demo alive and public repo are reported.
About text enumerates Home, Orders, Products, Customers, Analytics, Marketing, Routine Studio, and ten atomic tools.
impact_rationale: Merchants and operations teams repeatedly perform reporting workflows and could gain durable automation without waiting for developers to anticipate every routine.
impact_evidence: Packet targets commerce operations and weekly report generation.
Human review and allowed-input selection provide a plausible control point for learned routines.
creativity_rationale: Teaching an agent a new typed tool by demonstrating once in the real product is a genuinely original interaction model pursued deeply.
creativity_evidence: The project records semantic business actions rather than clicks/selectors.
A reviewed routine becomes the eleventh WebMCP tool and can be invoked with new inputs.
usability_note: Demonstration-based authoring could be approachable for merchants, but no visual evidence verifies the review experience.
red_flags: No video or gallery images; core end-to-end workflow is unobserved.
standouts: Human demonstration creates reusable typed agent capability.
Review and input-permission step addresses safety and drift.
advance_reason: One of the most original concepts in the packet and a strong example of WebMCP changing product capability.

one_line: CDN bridge that turns hosted MCP definitions into live browser WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Loads tool definitions from a Shredly-hosted MCP server and registers them in a site via a dependency-free ES module, with fresh per-user token callbacks.
leverage_rationale: It removes redeploy/code work from publishing browser tools and dynamically reflects hosted definitions in the page, a meaningful infrastructure-level WebMCP delta.
leverage_evidence: About text describes tools/list at page load followed by document.modelContext registration.
Adding a dashboard tool appears on the site automatically; fresh token callback supports per-user auth.
execution_rationale: The library concept and implementation outline are coherent, but there are no submitted frame sheets, no video, and only packaging evidence, so execution must be capped.
execution_evidence: Public repo, alive demo, and three gallery images are reported.
About text specifies plain ES module, no build step, no bundler, and no dependencies.
impact_rationale: Developers building MCP-backed products have a concrete deployment and maintenance pain that dynamic browser registration could reduce.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets hosting and managing MCP servers without infrastructure.
The bridge promises no redeploy/no code change for new site tools.
creativity_rationale: The hosted-to-browser bridge is a useful and somewhat original infrastructure packaging of WebMCP, though the underlying server-management category is established.
creativity_evidence: Dynamic propagation from a Shredly dashboard into live page tools is the distinctive angle.
Per-invocation token resolution handles late login and user context.
usability_note: A one-tag integration is potentially simple, but runtime errors, CORS, and tool schema behavior are not evidenced.
red_flags: No frame sheets submitted and no video; only packaging and claims support execution.
Core Shredly MCP-as-a-service predates the WebMCP bridge.
standouts: No-build CDN integration.
Fresh auth token callback for per-user browser context.
advance_reason: Potentially valuable infrastructure, but the packet lacks direct product-motion evidence and the novelty is narrower than leading entries.
